newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's rates four Chinese commercial banks.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates four Chinese commercial banks.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service on Thursday announced ratings for four Chinese commercial banks, CITIC Industrial Bank, China Merchants Bank, Guangdong Development Bank, and China Investment Bank.
Moody's assigned them each a long-term deposits rating of Baa3, a short-term deposits rating of Prime-3, a long-term debt rating of Baa3 and a bank financial strength rating of D.

Although the banking system remains dominated by four main state banks, commercial banks have received some encouragement from the central government and they are intended to provide both a model and a competitive spur to the far larger state banks, the rating agency said in a statement.

It said the commercial banks generally reflect the strong growth in China's economy -- their assets have grown rapidly and their loan quality has been reasonable, although profitability is still thin and their overall performance has been somewhat erratic.
Moody's said their efficiency and service quality were much higher than the state banks.
Commercial banks' asset quality was significantly better than the state banks', it added.

While the recent credit squeeze and the ever-growing need of China's deeply troubled state enterprises for cash may put more pressure on the commercial banks, the commercial groups associated with the banks being rated were themselves financially strong, Moody's said.

Operating costs in China's banking system were surprisingly high partly because of the current phase of heavy investment in the business. But the present financial condition of the larger commerical banks apperared sound, thanks partly to the buoyancy in the sectors of the economy in which they operate, Moody's said.
Beijing-based CITIC Industrial Bank, wholly owned by China International Trust & Investment Corp (CITIC), has 44 percent of its assets denominated in foreign currencies, Moody's said.
Its foreign currency loans have longer terms, and are funded mostly with borrowings from its parent CITIC, the agency added.

Its domestic currency assets and liabilities are short-term, while its asset mix contains a high propertion of securities, and a correspondingly low proportion of loans. Moody's said that helped overall asset quality and liquidity to the extent permitted by the limited depth of local securities markets.
It had total assets of 86.5 billion yuan at the end of 1995.
China Merchants Bank is controlled by China's Ministry of Communications.
Guangdong Development Bank is owned by a large number of the provincial and local authorities in Guangdong province.
China Investment Bank is wholly-owned by China Construction Bank, a major state bank.
